findings.body:
**Force a failure status when Git output exceeds the bound.**

At `src/adapters/crq/gitExec.ts:127`, `overflow` does not change `code`. Git can exit successfully before buffered stdout finishes draining. Killing the exited process does not change its exit status. Node documents that process exit and stream closure are separate events. ([nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html?utm_source=openai))

In that sequence, this returns `code: 0` with empty stdout. `gitOk` then accepts the discarded output as a successful read. Set a non-success status when `overflow` is true, or expose an explicit failure discriminator.
findings.title: Force a failure status when Git output exceeds the bound.

findings.body:
**Remove `--foreground` so `timeout` signals the review command's whole process group.**

`--foreground` at `src/adapters/crq/reviewProcess.ts:162` stops `timeout` from creating a separate process group. When the deadline expires, `timeout` signals only the direct review command. Background work that the command starts can keep running after `timeout` exits. The run still records completion from the direct child's exit, so that work can continue past the review deadline. This applies to any review command that starts background processes, such as `sh -c 'sleep 3600 & wait'`.

Remove the flag so `timeout` runs the command in its own process group and signals the group on timeout. The review child runs in a detached session, so it has no controlling terminal that needs foreground access. Processes that create their own process group still escape this signal, so the change narrows the gap but does not guarantee cleanup.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-        ['--foreground', '--kill-after=60', `${options.timeoutMinutes}m`, ...meta.cmd],
+        ['--kill-after=60', `${options.timeoutMinutes}m`, ...meta.cmd],
```

</details>
findings.title: Remove `--foreground` so `timeout` signals the review command's whole process group.

findings.body:
**Treat a zero-byte gitleaks report as a failed scan.**

At `src/adapters/crq/reviewGitleaks.ts:62`, the `|| '[]'` fallback turns a zero-byte report into an empty hit list. If gitleaks exits 0 and leaves a zero-byte `report.json`, the adapter returns `hits: []`. `src/queue-runner/reviewScan.ts:134-143` then records that as a clean scan, even though the file contains no JSON evidence. The `ReviewScannerEffects` contract at `src/queue-runner/reviewScan.ts:27` states that errors and missing reports cannot become clean. The sibling pre-upload scan in `src/ops/dev/denylist.ts:594-600` applies the same rule: an exit-0 run without a readable report is a fault.

Remove the fallback. A zero-byte report then fails `JSON.parse` inside the existing `try`, and the generic error path rejects the scan. A report that contains `[]` still returns a clean result.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-          new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }).decode(buffer.subarray(0, bytesRead)) || '[]',
+          new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }).decode(buffer.subarray(0, bytesRead)),
```

</details>
findings.title: Treat a zero-byte gitleaks report as a failed scan.

findings.body:
**Stop the spawned review when the post-spawn identity write fails.**

If `save(pidPath, { ...identity, cli_pid: child.pid })` rejects, `runReviewChild` rejects and the review keeps running. The inner and outer `finally` blocks close only the parent's log handles. Nothing kills the child or awaits `finished` on this path, so no `exit.json` is written. The `cli_pid` field also stays missing from the pidfile.

Once the child exits, the run is reported `ambiguous` rather than `harvest`, so its result is not recorded. The child stays bounded by `timeout`. Before the child exits, the run is reported `alive`, so it is not harvested early.

Before rethrowing, terminate the spawned `timeout` child with `child.kill(...)` and await `finished`. Do not signal the process group. The wrapper shares that group, so a group signal can also stop the wrapper.
findings.title: Stop the spawned review when the post-spawn identity write fails.
